reasoning: The one finding of the first round is closed: the requirement no longer claims the excluded fixtures are scanned, and every word of it is asserted by the change's single test.

simpler.evidence: design.md Decisions weighs three simpler routes: `detect-secrets scan` (walks the tree itself, no argv), in-process `pre_commit_hook.main(targets)` (no argv limit at all), and batching by a fixed file count. The first two are rejected by the scenario's own outcome — the gate must exit non-zero on a finding — and by the `-X utf8` Windows/Linux parity the `_secrets_cmd` comment records (ci_check.py:232-240); the third by variable path length. What is left is the minimum: one module-level constant and one packing helper inside the existing `check_secrets`, no abstraction with a second caller, two edited files in the proposal's Impact.

map.evidence: The delta carries one scenario, `implementation` / `Targets beyond one command line`; tasks.md's map points it at `tests/agent_process/test_ci_check.py::test_targets_beyond_one_command_line`, which task 1.1 writes. No scenario is unmapped and no map line lacks a scenario.

red.evidence: Group 1 (task 1.1) precedes the code of group 2 and fails in the test body on today's code: `check_secrets` makes exactly one `_run` call (ci_check.py:198), so the "more than one command was recorded" assertion fails on the single recorded command. The gate form matches the archived changes and the script's CLI (`check_red.py` takes node ids, check_red.py:167), and the RED commit is named.

platform.evidence: Two behaviours carry the design: the 32767-character `CreateProcess` command line and `list2cmdline` being the string `subprocess` hands it. The proposal records the reproduction at c50e7eb (WinError 206); I re-measured on today's tree — `_secrets_targets(_tracked_files())` is 490 and `len(subprocess.list2cmdline(_secrets_cmd(targets)))` is 33135, so with `_CMDLINE_LIMIT = 32000` today's tree already needs two batches and Linux CI exercises the multi-batch path the design relies on. The rejected `detect-secrets scan` alternative now carries the observation instead of an assertion: `python -m detect_secrets scan <dir>` exits 0 where `python -X utf8 -m detect_secrets.pre_commit_hook <file with AKIA...>` exits 1, which is the run I made in the first round, and the loose fixture-exclusion clause is gone.

replaced.evidence: One input is replaced: the single `_run(_secrets_cmd(targets))` becomes one `_run` per batch. Each guard that call carried is named and kept — the empty-list refusal (proposal What Changes, task 2.1), `_run`'s exit-on-first-failure (design, "Fail fast on the first failing batch"), and `-X utf8` with no `--baseline`, untouched because every batch goes through the same `_secrets_cmd`. The one input batching cannot serve, a single path longer than the limit, is in Risks with its failure mode stated: a batch of its own and the OS error as today, not a silent skip.

catcher.evidence: Every named catcher reaches a delivery step: `check_red.py` -> the RED commit (1.1); pytest plus `ci_check.py --only secrets` run on Windows -> the failure issue 231 actually reports, which the monkeypatched unit test cannot reach (2.1); `openspec validate --strict --all` and the full `ci_check.py` -> group 3; `wait_for_pr.py` with the agent-review rounds and the three-round escalation -> 4.3. The sibling argv-from-file-list call sites need no catcher here: I measured `check_module_size`'s pylint command at 804 characters over 50 modules against the same 32000 limit, so the growth this bug follows (one more tracked file per archived change, 490 today) does not reach them.

length.evidence: The plan adds one requirement title (8 words), one requirement sentence (38 words) and one scenario (three clauses), and task 1.1 asserts each: "scan every target it selects" -> the paths after the `_secrets_cmd` prefix of every command, concatenated, equal the 600 targets in order; "no command line it starts exceeds 32767" -> `len(subprocess.list2cmdline(cmd)) <= 32767` per recorded command; "fail when any batch reports a finding" -> `SystemExit` code 1 from the stub that fails the command holding the last path. The title now names the guarantee (the command-line limit) instead of a coverage the `_CAPTURED_HTML_FIXTURES` exclusion (ci_check.py:180, 228-229) contradicts, so it survives the archive as a stable identity; the proposal's Capabilities line was moved with it.

bespoke.evidence: The plan adds no script, check or workflow: `_CMDLINE_LIMIT` and the packing helper are private additions inside the existing `secrets` check of `.agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py`, and the proposal's Impact adds only the change directory. The standards for the job — the tool's own tree walk (`detect-secrets scan`) and the in-process entry point — are named in design.md Decisions with why each does not fit.
